conclusion: No explicit token-stealing payload or unexplained application-specific native modification identified in this DMG. Incident entry point and whether an earlier artifact was compromised remain unestablished.
basis: Independent static extraction, source/call-path review, native disassembly and upstream binary comparisons. Atomscan and VirusTotal verdicts were not used as evidence of absence.

native.normalization: Remove LC_CODE_SIGNATURE and adjust header command counts; normalize __LINKEDIT vmsize/filesize changed by signing; permit only 0-15 zero bytes to the exact 16-byte signature boundary. All remaining bytes match. Includes 13 Electron 44.4.5 files and two @lydell/node-pty-darwin-x64 1.2.0-beta.12 files.
native.cli_runtime: All 16 native runtime code/data sections match public Bun 1.4.2. The __BUN application graph is separate. Dyld chained-fixup/export-trie/function-start/data-in-code payloads match; their offsets shift by the inserted application segment.

direct_reverse_engineering.finding: Entire 161-byte spawn-helper text reviewed: acquire controlling TTY via ttyname/open/close, optional argv[1] chdir, execvp(argv[2], &argv[2]); error exits. node-pty exported paths validate caller arguments, use posix_openpt/grantpt/unlockpt, duplicate slave descriptors, and posix_spawn the helper with caller-supplied argv/env. Other exports use openpty and ioctl resize; init registers four JS functions. Evidence also includes node-pty-exports.txt.

Socket path comes from WATCHMAN_SOCK or watchman --output-encoding=bser get-sockname. Constructor builds AF_UNIX socket, then connects to that path. Module initializers register NAPI exports and initialize containers/mutex destructors.

Reviewed all eight FFI exports and source at npm gitHead a582ae17cc6c41cb890b142c48669936541339c7. Caller supplies command, cwd and environment. openpty/spawn and worker threads implement terminal read/write, process wait, resize, kill, handle and pending-buffer management. No socket/connect imports in this library.

Reviewed executable entry and service connect/send/receive paths with JS callers. Application connection is an AF_UNIX runtime-directory socket using service.json discovery and token-authenticated protocol 7; JS writes service metadata with mode 0600. Generic Rust network routines are also linked.

Reviewed instance initialization and network import callers. workerLoop belongs to filesystem walker indexing. connect callers examined are linked Zig standard I/O routines, including Unix/IP connect; presence alone does not establish a credential/exfiltration flow.

Reviewed selected execve/socket/connect wrappers and FFI/API surface. Includes terminal rendering, clipboard/audio/file functionality and Zig I/O runtime. Raw socket/process imports are present; no credential-to-network path was established. Rizin could not parse its LC_FUNCTION_STARTS, so CFG recovery was incomplete.

javascript.extraction: ASAR contents, 612-entry Bun module graph, and 1687 nested Brotli assets extracted without launching the sample.
javascript.method: Acorn syntax inventory of credential-related literals, network/process calls, dynamic imports and decoding; formatted 1219 main/preload/CLI modules plus seven selected renderer chunks. Manually traced the high-value flows below. This count is automated survey coverage, not a claim to have manually read every file or computed complete taint flow.

reviewed_flows.finding: Local credential JSON values in SQLite and legacy auth.json migration. Credential create/update logs examined carry IDs/type rather than token values.

Selected credential is resolved for its integration and passed to the provider package; Anthropic default requests use api.anthropic.com with x-api-key. Provider-specific OAuth/refresh and AWS/Google credential loaders were also examined. Configurable endpoints remain trusted runtime inputs.
Config GET carries the active Console bearer credential and optional org ID. This path does not enumerate and upload all locally stored external-provider keys.

Console response can supply package names, provider/model settings and headers. Selected-model resolution can install a package and dynamically import its JavaScript in the CLI process. ignoreScripts:true only disables npm lifecycle scripts. This is a possible runtime delivery path if the trusted config endpoint or a provider package is compromised; no malicious response/package attributable to this incident was obtained.

Desktop renderer sends Sentry error reports; no explicit provider-key upload was found in its initialization or reviewed capture paths. Error contents could still contain incidental sensitive data. Native crash upload is disabled at the inspected initialization. CLI OTLP exporters require an explicitly configured endpoint.

Preload surface and isolated renderer reviewed. Local service defaults to loopback with a generated password. Auth middleware validates Basic/cookie credentials; CORS does not itself bypass authentication.

Reviewed installed-extension code loading, archive path validation, official updater requests, browser proxy requests and OpenTunnel SDK. These have legitimate network/process capabilities; no automatic provider-secret harvest/upload was identified in the paths reviewed.

wasm.scope: Reviewed imports and relevant JS glue, not a decompilation of WASM algorithms. No direct fetch/socket/file-read/credential-storage import observed; some modules expose logging, callbacks, image/DOM operations or WASI fd_write.

incident_interpretation: A credential-store or gateway compromise on Console could expose server-held linked provider credentials without modifying this DMG; this remains a hypothesis based on the service architecture.

A compromised Console config response or dynamically installed provider package is another concrete trust path into an unchanged app; the code establishes capability, not evidence that it was exercised.
This sample alone cannot establish whether a previous desktop/npm release, an extension, runtime configuration, or a backend was the incident entry point.
limitations: Accompanying cached JavaScriptCore/Bun bytecode was not independently decompiled or proven semantically equivalent to the extracted source.

Native upstream comparison rules out per-app changes within the compared bytes; it does not establish that upstream packages themselves are free of vulnerabilities or malicious behavior. No independent reproducible source builds were performed.

Disassembly focused on entrypoints, constructors, FFI exports and credential/network/process-related paths. Every instruction of Electron, Bun and native dependencies was not manually reviewed; indirect dispatch and CFG recovery limit static coverage.

No execution of the application, live authenticated config capture, incident-time traffic, backend source/logs or earlier compromised artifact was available. No historical-compromise or current-service safety verdict follows.
Static source inventory and literal endpoint searches cannot exclude runtime-generated destinations, configuration abuse, incidental telemetry leakage or code loaded after installation.
